title: [source-postgres] Change Data Capture (CDC) Not Working
body:
### Topic

I have enabled Change Data Capture (CDC) on my PostgreSQL source following the instructions provided in the Airbyte PostgreSQL source documentation. However, during each sync, Airbyte is loading the entire dataset instead of only the changes. This issue persists even when there are no updates in the source database.

### Relevant information

**Steps Taken:**
  - Enabled logical replication in PostgreSQL.
  - Created a replication slot and a publication as per the documentation.
  - Set max_slot_wal_keep_size, max_wal_size, and wal_keep_size to 10GB.
  - Verified that CDC is correctly configured on the PostgreSQL side.

**Logs**:This 4th time ran sync log[default_workspace_logs_1388_txt.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17542553/default_workspace_logs_1388_txt.txt)

**Expected Behavior:**
Airbyte should only sync the changed records instead of reloading the entire dataset on every sync.

**Actual Behavior:**
Each sync loads the whole dataset, resulting in increased load times and performance issues.

**Additional Information:**
PostgreSQL Version: 16
Airbyte Version: 0.58.0 >


**Questions:**

1. What could be the underlying cause of the incremental changes not being detected?
2. Are there specific logs or configurations I should examine to troubleshoot this issue?

I would appreciate any assistance in diagnosing and resolving this problem.

comments.author: rodireich
comments.body:
The above log [provided](https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/issues/47547#issue-2618334320) by @Nanagoud007 is showing that the last saved offset is no longer on the database server and as a result we are falling back to rebuilding the tables from scratch :
```
2024-10-28 10:04:37 [44msource[0m > WARN main i.a.i.s.p.c.PostgresCdcCtidInitializer(cdcCtidIteratorsCombined):188 Saved offset is before Replication slot's confirmed_flush_lsn, Airbyte will trigger sync from scratch
```

Postgres has a retention period for CDC logs. In order for CDC based incremental sync to function we need Airbyte's sync timeout to be shorter than the retention period so postgres won't recycle the CDC logs we need before airbyte has a chance to read them.
Is this happening on every attempt to sync?

comments.author: rodireich
comments.body:
@jduckwo the first sync is actually done by going to the table and selecting from it. not some CDC operation.
Think of it essentially as a `SELECT * from table`.
The second sync is the one where we attempt to find our place in the CDC log (or WAL in postgres) and in your case if it fails immediately after the first sync it indicates that something is misconfigured.
On the log you provided I don't see the same problem with an offset no longer on server. But maybe that log doesn't cover the second sync.

comments.author: rowanmoul
comments.body:
We've started having a very similar problem since upgrading to Postgres 16 last week (previously we were using 14). For the upgrade, the replication slots needed to be dropped of course, but after re-creating them and selecting "clear data" in the connections, subsequent syncs keep failing with the the "Saved offset is before replication slot's confirmed lsn" error. Nothing else has changed. 
The `max_slot_wal_keep_size` is set to the default of `-1` (infinite) and the disk is not full, so there is no reason why it should be out of sync. Nothing else is using this replication slot. We are only syncing once per day, but this was never a problem before now since there is no limit on the amount of WAL logs being kept (aside from the disk size, which never gets full)

Steps taken following the upgrade and dropping of replication slots:
1. Re-create replication slots for each connection with identical settings as before.
2. Run "clear data" on the connection
3. Sync (initial sync, pulls all data)
4. Sync again - FAIL - _Saved offset is before replication slot's confirmed lsn_

Edit:
I also just tried changing `InvalidCdcCursorPositionBehaviour` to "Re-sync Data" and this allowed the sync to succeed, however runnng the sync a second time immediately after the first one shows the same warning message (_Saved offset is before Replication slot's confirmed_flush_lsn, Airbyte will trigger sync from scratch_), which tells me that had `InvalidCdcCursorPositionBehaviour` been set to "Fail sync", it would have indeed failed.

*We are running the latest Airbyte 1.2 via Helm Chart, and the latest versions of all the connectors.

comments.author: rowanmoul
comments.body:
I've been digging WAY too deep into this, and it looks like the final CDC state isn't being saved in some cases, but I can't figure out why. The final state is logged during the save process on each sync:
```
source > INFO main i.a.i.s.p.c.PostgresCdcStateHandler(saveState):38 debezium state: {"[\"redacted\",{\"server\":\"redacted\"}]":"{\"transaction_id\":null,\"lsn\":1950553113328,\"txId\":266233230,\"ts_usec\":1732059523586293}"}
source > INFO main i.a.c.i.s.r.s.SourceStateIterator(computeNext):84 sending final state message, with count per stream: {}
```
But on connections that are not working as described in my previous comment, the value printed in this log line is NOT the value saved to the airbyte database. The value that is saved is... _"before Replication slot's confirmed_flush_lsn"_, but the value printed in the log is NOT.

----
Somehow I have managed to get some connections to work again by running a sync once with "Re-Sync Data" set on the source, and subsequent syncs continue to work (with `InvalidCdcCursorPositionBehaviour` set to "Fail Sync" again). In these cases, the logs are slightly different:
```
source > INFO main i.a.i.s.p.c.PostgresCdcStateHandler(saveState):38 debezium state: {"[\"redacted\",{\"server\":\"redacted\"}]":"{\"lsn_proc\":1980886834104,\"messageType\":\"INSERT\",\"lsn_commit\":1980886097776,\"lsn\":1980886834104,\"txId\":269703434,\"ts_usec\":1732574595236910}"}
source > INFO main i.a.c.i.s.r.s.SourceStateIterator(computeNext):84 sending final state message, with count per stream: {redacted large list of streams and counts}
```
Not only is the state data slightly different (and actually saved to the airbyte database), but the "final state message" actually lists the counts per stream, as opposed to the blank line in the first example.


Perhaps this is enough of a clue for someone who actually knows how the postgres source connector works to find the problem? I'd be happy to share full log files privately via Slack.

comments.author: rowanmoul
comments.body:
The differences in behaviour and state described in my previous post seem to be connected to whether or not there is any changes to the database between when the sync starts and ends. On databases with consistent traffic, there is no problem, but on databases with zero traffic during the sync, Airbyte/debezium appears to complete the re-sync, then sit and wait for a change to happen and then after 120 "puts" it quitely gives up and completes the sync as "successful" without recording the final state, causing the next sync to fail (or re-sync again) due to the saved LSN being before the slot's confirmed flush LSN.
Sample logs:
```
2024-11-28 22:14:00 source > INFO pool-2-thread-1 i.a.c.i.d.AirbyteDebeziumHandler$CapacityReportingBlockingQueue(reportQueueUtilization):48 CDC events queue stats: size=0, cap=10000, puts=117, polls=0
2024-11-28 22:14:00 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):87 CDC events queue poll(): blocked for PT10.522608394S after its previous call which was also logged.
2024-11-28 22:14:00 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):140 CDC events queue poll(): returned a heartbeat event: no progress since last heartbeat.
2024-11-28 22:14:10 source > INFO pool-2-thread-1 i.a.c.i.d.AirbyteDebeziumHandler$CapacityReportingBlockingQueue(reportQueueUtilization):48 CDC events queue stats: size=0, cap=10000, puts=118, polls=0
2024-11-28 22:14:10 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):87 CDC events queue poll(): blocked for PT10.021465577S after its previous call which was also logged.
2024-11-28 22:14:10 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):140 CDC events queue poll(): returned a heartbeat event: no progress since last heartbeat.

2024-11-28 22:14:20 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):87 CDC events queue poll(): blocked for PT10.021492157S after its previous call which was also logged.
2024-11-28 22:14:20 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):140 CDC events queue poll(): returned a heartbeat event: no progress since last heartbeat.
2024-11-28 22:14:30 source > INFO pool-2-thread-1 i.a.c.i.d.AirbyteDebeziumHandler$CapacityReportingBlockingQueue(reportQueueUtilization):48 CDC events queue stats: size=0, cap=10000, puts=120, polls=0
2024-11-28 22:14:30 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):87 CDC events queue poll(): blocked for PT10.02233072S after its previous call which was also logged.
2024-11-28 22:14:30 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):140 CDC events queue poll(): returned a heartbeat event: no progress since last heartbeat.
2024-11-28 22:14:30 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(requestClose):275 Closing: Heartbeat indicates sync is not progressing
```

A work around for this issue appears to be the Debezium Heartbeat Query in the source settings.
[The documentation](https://docs.airbyte.com/integrations/sources/postgres/postgres-troubleshooting#advanced-wal-disk-consumption-and-heartbeat-action-query) suggests this is only needed for a specific issue with disk usage spikes, but setting a query to update a table that is part of the Publication appears to "force" an update on low traffic databases and allow the sync to succeed (and save the final state). In my case, I created a special table with datetime column, and set the query in the airbyte source to update the column's value to `now()` whenever it runs.
Sample Logs:
```
2024-11-28 23:34:05 source > INFO pool-2-thread-1 i.d.c.c.BaseSourceTask(logStatistics):323 1 records sent during previous 00:00:12.277, last recorded offset of {server=redacted} partition is {lsn=2000066412936, txId=271489410, ts_usec=1732835849309056}

2024-11-28 23:34:05 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):87 CDC events queue poll(): blocked for PT12.693975043S in its first call.
2024-11-28 23:34:05 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):140 CDC events queue poll(): returned a heartbeat event: progressing to 2000066412936.
2024-11-28 23:34:15 source > INFO pool-2-thread-1 i.d.c.c.BaseSourceTask(logStatistics):323 1 records sent during previous 00:00:10.044, last recorded offset of {server=redacted} partition is {lsn_proc=2000148179280, messageType=NOOP, lsn_commit=2000148179280, lsn=2000148179280, txId=271496815, ts_usec=1732836845586001}
2024-11-28 23:34:15 source > INFO pool-2-thread-1 i.a.c.i.d.AirbyteDebeziumHandler$CapacityReportingBlockingQueue(reportQueueUtilization):48 CDC events queue stats: size=0, cap=10000, puts=2, polls=0
2024-11-28 23:34:15 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):87 CDC events queue poll(): blocked for PT10.035974086S after its previous call which was also logged.
2024-11-28 23:34:15 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(computeNext):140 CDC events queue poll(): returned a heartbeat event: progressing to 2000148179280.
2024-11-28 23:34:15 source > INFO main i.a.i.s.p.c.PostgresCdcTargetPosition(reachedTargetPosition):80 Signalling close because heartbeat LSN : 2000148179280 is after target LSN : PgLsn{lsn=2000066422912}
2024-11-28 23:34:15 source > INFO main i.a.c.i.d.i.DebeziumRecordIterator(requestClose):275 Closing: Heartbeat indicates sync is done by reaching the target position
```

I can reliably reproduce the above behaviour in our test environment.

_I also had one instance where having a stream (table) selected in the connection that was not part of the Publication caused the final state to not be recorded in the Airbyte DB, despite the sync otherwise succeeding (as per the second set of logs). I have not tried to reproduce this case._

comments.author: ssay-work
comments.body: I ran into this same problem, did you implement the heartbeat workaround @rowanmoul ? Did that alleviate the issue?

comments.author: rowanmoul
comments.body:
Yes, the heartbeat appears to have alleviated the issue entirely for us.
How to add a heartbeat table:
1. Create a simple table - I had columns "id", "value", and "updated", though I could have skipped the "value" column in hindsight
2. Add this table to the publication  - *this is critical*
3. Put a query like this into the debezium heartbeat query field in the source: `update yourSchema.yourTable set value='heartbeat', updated=now();`
You do NOT need to replicate this stream in airbyte for this to work. In fact we don't have the schema this table is in selected in the source configuration.

This is definitely just a workaround though. There is clear underlying problem that should be addressed. I'm not sure if it's a problem with Airbyte, Debezium, or both.

comments.author: FVidalCarneiro
comments.body:
@Nanagoud007 , we are also facing issues with this connector, but different to these. The error we are experiencing is:
```
Saved offset is before replication slot's confirmed lsn. Please reset the connection, and then increase WAL retention and/or increase sync frequency to prevent this from happening in the future. See https://docs.airbyte.com/integrations/sources/postgres/postgres-troubleshooting#under-cdc-incremental-mode-there-are-still-full-refresh-syncs for more details.
```
On our end, versions of the connector superior to `3.6.15` fail with this error.

Fo your issue however, I would suggest chcking two things:
- Do your tables have primary keys?
- Have you tried downgrading to this version?

If you are facing the same issue as me, you can also refer to this issue (https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/issues/55846)
